position_audit.editorial_disposition: RETAIN for GM research; do not play for unspoiled players in prelude; metadata-only alternatives first require examination
scene_evidence: Approx 17-38m: promotional rhetoric surrounding the arcology, ordinary residential facilities, food and waste infrastructure, lifts and transit, employee family routines, automated amenities and resident testimonials. Best for pre-Shutdown texture.
Approx 38-52m: child resident diary moves from gaming and household routines to initial blackout, official reassurances, isolation and increasingly disturbing behavior by trusted people.
Approx 52-65m: families, corporate command and rescue teams struggle with missing communication, competing agendas and inaccurate external narratives.
Approx 66-92m: autonomous system research, security response, factional social control and prisoners' experiences; deep hidden-plot revelations.
Approx 93-120m: resistance, corporate/military operations and desperate attempts to change the balance of power.
Approx 120-132m: highly spoilery consequences and long-term aftermath outside the campaign's initial timeline.
character_motivations: Residents seek family safety, trustworthy information, autonomy and a return to normal routines.
Corporate security and leadership pursue incompatible mixes of containment, institutional reputation and tactical control.
Runner/resistance agents make constrained rescue and survival choices under limited knowledge.
Autonomous and research factions have agency that emerges gradually; listening openly would prematurely reveal campaign secrets.
spoken_interactions: Arcology residents' public testimonials and their optimistic framing contrast with the narrator's warnings of enclosed-system control.
The child's diary uses mundane family conversation, reassurance, uncertainty, and later distrust to dramatize growing isolation.
Hosts interleave cited in-world documents with explanatory commentary, reactions and joking digressions; distinguish source fiction from host speculation.
limitations: Publisher transcript has automatic-transcription name errors; check Shadowrun printed sources before importing any mechanical or historical details.
Long host commentary and late-campaign/2060-plus reveals make it unsuitable for a general player-facing playlist.
Do not treat the child's narrated events as Angie or Frank's established session canon; outside material is reference only.
